blocks.text: A kidney transplant is surgery in which a person's non-functioning kidney is replaced with a healthy kidney from a donor. It is offered to people with end-stage kidney failure, and needs careful evaluation, matching and monitoring for the best results for both recipient and donor.

blocks.caption: Potential donors
rows: a person genetically related to the recipient, such as a parent, sibling or child; can be the best donor
not genetically related, such as a spouse, friend or co-worker; less common, but can succeed if blood group and tissue type match
people who register with hospitals to donate organs after death; their kidneys are matched by blood group, tissue type and immune compatibility

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: Kidney donation can be a life-saving gift for someone with end-stage kidney disease. The book notes that donating a kidney has no significant long-term health risk for the donor and that studies show donors' overall health and lifespan are generally unaffected.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: Pakistan's first kidney transplant centre was set up in 1985 at the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation (SIUT), Karachi, which the book calls one of the largest and most successful transplant centres in the world. The Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Center (PKLI&RC), a tertiary-care hospital in Lahore, was set up in 2017 to tackle kidney and liver disease through care, transplantation and research.

items: Rejection: the recipient's immune system may recognise the new kidney as foreign and attack it, even when the patient takes immunosuppressant medicines.
Infection: patients whose immune system is suppressed are at higher risk of infections after the transplant.
Side effects of immunosuppressants, given to prevent rejection: high blood pressure, weight gain and a higher risk of infections and cancers.

blocks.prompt: Why are kidney transplant patients prescribed immunosuppressant drugs, and what is the cost?
blocks.explanation: To stop the immune system rejecting the donated kidney as foreign. The cost is a weaker defence: more infections and cancers, plus side effects such as high blood pressure and weight gain.

items: Transplant replaces a failed kidney (end-stage failure); donors: related, unrelated, deceased, matched by blood group and tissue type.
Problems: rejection, infection, immunosuppressant side effects. SIUT Karachi 1985; PKLI&RC Lahore 2017.
